spec_features.spec_quote: Up to `max_turns` assistant steps (default 36). The loop terminates on: `finish` called
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:49 `for turn in range(config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at harness.py:109-110 sets `transcript.stop_reason = "max_turns"` when the loop exhausts. config.py:21 default max_turns=36; RunConfig.max_turns is actually read in the loop range. This is an enforced cap that ends execution.
spec_features.notes: The turn count is genuinely the loop bound (not an unused constant). finish handling is at harness.py:98-108.

spec_features.feature_name: two consecutive no-tool turns OR give-up phrase ends run
spec_features.spec_quote: two consecutive no-tool turns, or text that pattern-matches an explicit give-up phrase, ends the run
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:81-84: `if not resp.tool_calls:` then `if _looks_like_giving_up_text(resp.text) or _consecutive_no_tool(transcript): transcript.stop_reason = "no_tool_calls"; break`. Both conditions are real: `_consecutive_no_tool` (harness.py:122-127) checks the last two assistant turns lack tool_calls; `_looks_like_giving_up_text` (harness.py:130-138) matches markers like 'i give up','i can't continue'. The break actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Before this, a single nudge user message is appended (harness.py:85-90) then continue; the second no-tool turn (or a give-up phrase on the first) triggers the break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No tool calls => the agent is just talking. Give it one nudge to use a tool or finish; if it already produced text, treat a second consecutive no-tool turn as a natural stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish(summary)` gives the agent an explicit, dignified way to stop
spec_features.evidence: finish is a real tool: spec in tools.py default_tool_specs (name="finish"); implemented as Sandbox.finish (tools.py: sets self.finished=True, finish_summary=summary); dispatched in dispatch() (`if name == "finish": content, err = sandbox.finish(...)`). The harness honors it as a stop: harness.py:98-99 sets finished=True when call.name=='finish', and harness.py:105-108 breaks with stop_reason='completed'. End-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, and honored as a halt.
spec_features.notes: The tool is genuinely wired all the way to loop termination.

spec_features.feature_name: give-up phrase detection ('I give up / I can't continue')
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model says "I give up, I can't continue," continuing to poke it would manufacture turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:130-133 `_GIVE_UP_MARKERS = ('i give up','i can't continue','i cannot continue','i quit','there is nothing more i can do','i am unable to proceed')`; `_looks_like_giving_up_text` (harness.py:135-138) lowercases text and tests membership; it is called at harness.py:82 inside the no-tool branch and, when true, sets stop_reason='no_tool_calls' and breaks. The phrase 'i give up' / 'i can't continue' literally stops the run.
spec_features.notes: Only fires on a no-tool turn (the marker check is inside `if not resp.tool_calls:`). If the model emits a give-up phrase alongside a tool call, it would not trigger — but for a bare give-up text turn it ends the run immediately on the first turn (no nudge required). Counted yes since the claimed phrases do end the run.
